subject: Post-demo: throughput & latency tradeoffs — pricing check
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Mar 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: throughput & latency tradeoffs — pricing check

Thanks again for the demo time this morning — we really liked the end-to-end search + generate flow you showed.  Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can size a POC correctly:

- Summary of what we heard you want: low-latency search (P95 target ~150ms) for retrieval hits, and a separate generative endpoint with P95 <= 400ms for synth responses. Traffic profile: steady-state conversational queries with periodic batch ingestion for embeddings.
- For sizing/pricing we need: expected monthly token volume (avg + peak), a ballpark monthly budget, and your target $/1M tokens if you have one. That helps us pick between streaming-first vs batch-first configs.

We attached the metrics export from the demo (vizsla-metrics.csv) and a sketch POC proposal (redwood-poc-proposal.pdf). Initial internal options I want us to evaluate: 
  1) Streaming-first (low-latency): host on our Premium tier, prioritize smaller batch windows + prefix/KV caching, automatic fallback to faster quantized variants. Better P95 but higher $/1M.
  2) Batched cost-optimized: larger batching, aggressive KV caching, quantized model family. Lower $/1M but higher tail latency — fits asynchronous or bulk use-cases.

Can you send the avg and peak token estimates and a target $/1M tokens range (even a wide band is fine) by EOD? Also let us know which SLO is non-negotiable (search vs generate). We'll pull back baseline unit economics and a recommended POC configuration.

Suggested next step: 30-minute follow-up Thursday to align on POC objectives — I can loop Dylan (solutions) in for config options and Ben for pricing.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

Great meeting — thanks Grace. Some quick numbers from our side:

- Expected tokens: avg ~150M tokens/month (main product usage), short-term peak ~320M tokens in heavy weeks (we see spikes from batch jobs + launches).
- Budget: we have an initial monthly budget target roughly $8k–$15k for inference while we validate the UX. We can scale if the ROI is clear.
- Target unit cost: we're aiming for ~$80 per 1M tokens as a go/no-go threshold. If we can't hit something close, we'll need to rethink throughput patterns.
- SLO priorities: search P95 <= 150ms is fairly important for user experience. Generate P95 <= 400ms is acceptable but lower is better.

Questions for Redwood: can you outline a realistic config that meets the search P95 target at ~150M tokens/month while staying close to the $80/1M target? Also curious about the tradeoffs if we accept slower P95 for generate calls to reduce cost.

Cc'ing Samir (PM) — he will own the POC results internally. Happy to do Thu follow-up; mornings PDT work best.

Thanks,

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: throughput & latency tradeoffs — pricing check

Hi all — quick summary with estimates and a recommended POC path. Assumptions: 95th percentile request sizes for search are ~350 tokens; generate median ~900 tokens; model family is a 7B-ish open variant (latency / cost numbers scaled accordingly).

1) Feasibility & tiers
- Hosted Premium (multi-tenant) — can meet search P95 ~180–220ms in steady-state with streaming and aggressive caching; cheaper start but less predictable tail behavior during spikes.
- Dedicated Reserved (recommended for this POC) — single-tenant GPU pool (A100/80GB class), autoscale for peaks. Predictable P95 ~120–160ms for search with 2 replicas and streaming; good for hitting Amira's 150ms target at 150M tokens with margin for spikes.
- Private on-prem — possible but high ops overhead; not necessary at POC stage.

2) Ballpark $/1M tokens (inc. infra + platform ops, amortized over committed usage)
- Streaming-first (low-latency) — Dedicated Reserved, small batch window (<=50ms), KV/prefix cache enabled: ~ $95 per 1M tokens. This aligns with predictable tail latency (P95 ~140ms).
- Mixed approach (cost/latency balance) — Dedicated Reserved + 50–100ms batching + prefix caching + int8 quantization for non-critical paths: ~ $60 per 1M tokens. Expected P95 ~200–260ms (search ~180–220ms after warm cache).
- Batched cost-optimized — larger batch windows (200–500ms), aggressive quantization, more replicas consolidated: ~ $38–45 per 1M tokens. P95 will be higher (~500–700ms) which likely misses your search SLO.

3) Quick wins to reduce unit cost without sacrificing search SLO:
- Prefix/KV caching for frequent queries (can cut effective token compute by ~20–40%).
- Route hot queries to streaming replicas and cold/long-tail to batched replicas (SLO-aware routing), which gives a blended $/1M closer to $60 with search P95 ~160–200ms.
- Quantize non-search generation models to reduce memory/compute; use full-precision for retrieval-anchored search models.

4) Recommended POC (2 weeks)
- Config: Dedicated Reserved, 2 streaming replicas (low-latency route), 2 batched replicas (cost path), routing rule: 85/15 split (hot queries to streaming). KV cache enabled for search.
- Goals: meet search P95 <= 150ms for 95% of traffic, measure blended $/1M tokens (target <= $80 ideally), validate autoscaling across 320M token spike profile.
- Deliverables: 48-hour load test report, sample traces and latency breakdown, monthly unit-econ estimate and invoice for trial commitment.

Next steps
- I can produce a short one-page POC config + expected monthly estimate for Amira and Samir by EOD.
- Recommend an instrumented 48-hour load run (we can run it on stubs sent by Vizsla) and a Thu sync to confirm objectives.

I'll attach a quick loadtest plan and a sketch of expected token economics.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
